conventions.bandwidth: per direction, B/s; NVIDIA prints NVLink as a bidirectional total, which is halved here. Ethernet and InfiniBand rates are per direction (full duplex).

m_dense_bf16.layout: TP8 prefill → TP8 decode: each GPU sends its own KV head's share on its own link; all flows run in parallel.

m_dense_fp8.layout: TP8 prefill → TP8 decode: each GPU sends its own KV head's share on its own link; all flows run in parallel.

k3_bf16_mla.layout: TEP8 prefill -> DEP16 decode, NIXL (vLLM validated topology). MLA KV is replicated on the TEP8 ranks, so one copy is sent; the KDA state is split by head across the prefill ranks. One DEP16 decode rank receives all of it, so its ingress link is the bottleneck.

k3_fp8_mla.layout: TEP8 prefill -> DEP16 decode, NIXL (vLLM validated topology). MLA KV is replicated on the TEP8 ranks, so one copy is sent; the KDA state is split by head across the prefill ranks. One DEP16 decode rank receives all of it, so its ingress link is the bottleneck.

nvlink4_h100.pairing: M-dense only if prefill and decode GPUs share one NVLink domain. An M-dense TP=8 replica fills a whole 8-GPU HGX node, so its prefill → decode path between nodes is the NIC.

nvlink5_gb300.pairing: K3 inside one GB300 NVL72 rack (reference architecture RA-55: KV moves by NIXL over NVLink).

per_direction.formula: 400 Gb/s / 8 bits per byte (full duplex: this rate in each direction)

ib_ndr_400g.scope: per GPU (one ConnectX-7 per GPU on DGX H100)
ib_ndr_400g.pairing: M-dense prefill node → decode node (GPUDirect RDMA).

gb300_nic_800g.pairing: K3 prefill and decode in different racks.

measured_effective.formula: Mooncake Transfer Engine measured total / NIC count (40 GB transfer, 4×200 Gbps RoCE (FAST 2025 §5.4.1))

roce_200g.scope: per GPU (Mooncake production: one 200 Gb/s RoCEv2 NIC per GPU)
roce_200g.pairing: A RoCE cluster such as Mooncake's.

tcp_25g_slow_path.scope: per node (one port shared by all GPUs of the node)
tcp_25g_slow_path.label: HYPOTHETICAL
tcp_25g_slow_path.pairing: A deployment without RDMA: KV goes through host memory and the kernel TCP stack.

layerwise_streaming_m_dense.model: M-dense, BF16 KV, TP=8 prefill → TP=8 decode
layerwise_streaming_m_dense.per_layer_compute_formula: [2 × params_per_layer × T + 2 × H × d_head × T × (T + 1)] / G_node
layerwise_streaming_m_dense.per_layer_bytes_formula: T × 2 × H_kv × d_head × 2 B (÷ TP per GPU link)
layerwise_streaming_m_dense.exposed_note: Layer i's KV is sent when layer i finishes; transfers queue on the link. If t_x ≤ t_c only the last layer's transfer is left after prefill ends. The lm_head and sampling after the last layer are not counted, so the exposed time is an upper bound.

min_context_fully_hidden.formula: smallest T with t_x(T) ≤ t_c(T): T + 1 ≥ (G_node × b / B − 2 × params_per_layer) / (2 × H × d_head)
min_context_fully_hidden.terms: b = KV bytes per token per layer on the bottleneck link, B = its per-direction bandwidth
min_context_fully_hidden.note: Per-layer compute grows as T² (attention) while per-layer transfer grows as T, so every link is hidden beyond some context length.

m_dense_h_teach.formula: prefill FLOPs / (8 × H100 BF16 dense × prefill_mfu)

k3_gb300_tep8_lower_bound.formula: (2 × active_params × T + causal MLA attention) / (8 × GB300 BF16 dense × prefill_mfu) (TEP8)
k3_gb300_tep8_lower_bound.note: KDA recurrence FLOPs are not counted, so this is a lower bound. The MoE runs in MXFP4/MXFP8, so the BF16 peak is a convention here.

rule.statement: Disaggregation pays when the KV transfer that cannot be hidden is shorter than one decode step; then a new request's TTFT grows by less than one token interval, while running decodes no longer wait behind a long prefill. Transfer erases the gain when moving the KV takes as long as computing it, i.e. bandwidth per GPU below the break-even kv_bytes_per_token_per_gpu / prefill_time_per_token (see kv_tiers.json crossover).
rule.numbers: M-dense, 32,768 tokens, BF16 KV: prefill 2630 ms; 400 Gb/s RDMA transfer 31.5 ms (2.3 ms exposed if streamed per layer), below the 60 ms TPOT SLO; the HYPOTHETICAL 25 Gb/s TCP path takes 3782 ms, 1.44× the prefill (1208 ms exposed if streamed; fully hidden only from 98,453 tokens).

dynamo_conditional_disaggregation.rule: Dynamo (off by default) prefills locally on the decode worker when the effective ISL is below 2,048 tokens and below 0.7 of the ISL.
